newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish mixed, long end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish mixed, long end higher.

text.p: Feb 28 - U.S. debt futures end mixed with the long end slightly higher on pre-weekend short-covering after steep losses this week. Short end under pressure from ideas the tone bearish into payrolls. Monday's June T-bond support at 110-1/32, resistance at 111-00, traders said. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuter.com))
"We saw some bidding the the last five years for us and I think the tens and 30s just had a little short-covering heading into the weekend," the Eurodollar manager said.
June T-bond support for early next week was pegged at Thursday's session low of 110-1/32 and at the 200-day moving average of 109-21/32, traders said.

June posted an inside day on bar charts Friday, meaning it remained with the boundaries of Thursday's trade. Often, such a technical formation is tied to consolidation after a steep move, technicians said.
"By and large the market still trades with a heavy tone looking towards next week," another debt trader said.
Traders noted that debt futures barely reacted to a downward revision in fourth-quarter GDP this morning and strong data had equally limited impact.

GDP growth was revised to 3.9 percent from the 4.7 percent preliminary estimate. Chicago Purchasing managers February index rose to 56.2 from 55.9 in January, and the final February University of Michigan consumer sentiment index was reported at 99.7 versus 97.4 in January.
January existing home sales rose 2.1 percent.
"The news this week is showing somewhat more strength than we have expected," said Evelina Tainer, chief economist of Indosuez Carr Futures, in her weekly commentary.
"Furthermore, the news coming up in the next couple of weeks is likely to be bearish for the fixed income market as well," she said.
She forecast a non-farm payrolls increase of 220,000 for February and said anything over 175,00 would portend a robust economy.
Payrolls will be released at 0730 CST/1330 GMT next Friday. On Wednesday, Humphrey-Hawkins testimony concludes.

At the close, June T-bonds were up 6/32 points at 110-14/32, 10-year notes rose 3/32 to 107-22/32, munis gained 1/32 to 114-07/32, June T-bills fell one basis point to 94.77, and June Eurodollars fell one to 94.21. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
